card.statement:
As for any $\infty$ -category of sheaves on an ind-scheme of ind-finite type, the $\infty$ -category $\mathsf{Shv}(\mathrm{Gr})$ carries a natural perverse t-structure associated with the middle perversity. The perverse t-structure on $\mathsf{Shv}(\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{u}}^{{\frac{\infty}{2}}}\backslash\mathrm{Gr})$ is however not a restriction of this t-structure. This is related to the fact that the $\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{u}}^{{\frac{\infty}{2}}}$ -orbits on $\mathrm{Gr}$ are infinite-dimensional, hence do not interact well with the usual game of perverse sheaves.

For any $\lambda\in\mathbf{Y}$ , one can also consider the $\infty$ -category $\mathsf{Shv}(\mathrm{S}_{\lambda})$ , and the full subcategory $\mathsf{Shv}(\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{u}}^{{\frac{\infty}{2}}}\backslash\mathrm{S}_{\lambda})\subset\mathsf{Shv}(\mathrm{S}_{\lambda})$ of complexes equivariant under the action of $\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{u}}^{{\frac{\infty}{2}}}$ ; here since the action is transitive we have a canonical equivalence

(5.7)

$\mathsf{Shv}(\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{u}}^{{\frac{\infty}{2}}}\backslash\mathrm{S}_{\lambda})\cong\mathsf{Vect}_{\Bbbk}$

induced by taking the $!$ -restriction to $[z^{\lambda}]$ , see [2, Eqn. (3.6)]. (In the right-hand side, $\mathsf{Vect}_{\Bbbk}$ is the $\infty$ -category of complexes of $\Bbbk$ -vector spaces.) Using this equivalence one can define a t-structure on $\mathsf{Shv}(\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{u}}^{{\frac{\infty}{2}}}\backslash\mathrm{S}_{\lambda})$ , by taking the cohomological shift of the transfer of the tautological t-structure on $\mathsf{Vect}_{\Bbbk}$ such that the complex $\omega_{\mathrm{S}_{\lambda}}[-\langle\lambda,2\rho\rangle]$ is perverse. (Here, $\omega_{\mathrm{S}_{\lambda}}$ is the dualizing complex on $\mathrm{S}_{\lambda}$ , obtained by $!$ -pullback from the sheaf $\Bbbk$ on a point; this complex corresponds to $\Bbbk$ under the equivalence (5.7).) The cohomology functors associated with this t-structure will be denoted $({}^{\mathrm{p}}\hskip-0.5pt\mathcal{H}^{n}:n\in\mathbb{Z})$ . Objects in its heart are direct sums of copies of $\omega_{\mathrm{S}_{\lambda}}[-\langle\lambda,2\rho\rangle]$ ; in case the multiplicity in an object $\mathcal{F}$ is finite we call it the rank of $\mathcal{F}$ , and denote it $\rank(\mathcal{F})$ .

We have canonical functors

$(\mathbf{i}_{\lambda})^{!}:\mathsf{Shv}(\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{u}}^{{\frac{\infty}{2}}}\backslash\mathrm{Gr})\to\mathsf{Shv}(\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{u}}^{{\frac{\infty}{2}}}\backslash\mathrm{S}_{\lambda}), (\mathbf{i}_{\lambda})^{*}:\mathsf{Shv}(\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{u}}^{{\frac{\infty}{2}}}\backslash\mathrm{Gr})\to\mathsf{Shv}(\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{u}}^{{\frac{\infty}{2}}}\backslash\mathrm{S}_{\lambda}).$

Recall also the $q$ -analogue of Kostant’s partition function $\mathcal{P}(\lambda,q)\in\mathbb{Z}[q]$ , which counts the number of ways to write $\lambda$ as a sum of positive roots; see [2, §6.7] for our normalization. The following statement is part of [2, Theorem 8.2].
card.label: Remark 5.7

paper.title: Modular intersection cohomology of Drinfeld's compactifications
paper.abstract: We compute the dimension of the cohomology of stalks of intersection cohomology complexes on Zastava schemes and Drinfeld compactifications associated with a connected reductive algebraic group $G$, in case the characteristic of the coefficients field $\Bbbk$ is good for $G$. In particular, we show that these dimensions do not depend on the choice of $\Bbbk$.
